deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): X_0 is a scheme over a perfect field k of characteristic p, and S = Spec W(k). Grothendieck had hoped that H^*((X_0/S)_cris, O) would be the right p-adic cohomology. Here 'cris' must be the nilpotent-thickening (infinitesimal) site without divided powers. With divided powers, Berthelot's comparison would give exactly H_DR(X/W) for a smooth proper lift, so the failure he describes could not occur. If X_0 is smooth and lifts to X smooth over W, this cohomology is lim_n of the cohomology of the truncations X_n/S_n. He hoped this would agree, perhaps modulo torsion, with lim_n H_DR(X_n/S_n) = H_DR(X/S). It does not. For an 'ordinary' smooth X_0 the groups vanish for i > dim X_0, which is Witt-vector-cohomology-like behaviour. The de Rham limit, by contrast, is excellent.

This page begins: 'Looking at the affine case, one sees that the trouble comes from the fact that the projective limit does not commute with localisation by p, W -> W[1/p] = K.' The diagnosis is that the p-adically completed (formal) objects are the wrong ones once p is inverted. In the infinitesimal setting the integration constants 1/(n+1) are needed for a Poincaré lemma, and they only make sense after inverting p. Completing first and then inverting p loses them.

Proposal: replace the crystalline site by a bigger site of 'pro-infinitesimal' thickenings by Washnitzer–Monsky (weakly complete) objects. The objects are triples (U_0, V, i) where:
- U_0 is an affine open of X_0 with ring A_0;
- V is a 'W-M affine over W', i.e. Spec of a W-M (weakly complete, finitely generated) W-algebra B;
- i: U_0 -> V induces a nilpotent immersion of U_0 into the reduction V ⊗ k.
Algebraically, i is a surjective W-homomorphism B -> A_0 such that B/pB -> A_0 has nilpotent kernel. The topology is a suitable variant of the Zariski topology, generated by coverings coming from traces of opens of X_0.

The next page states the 'decisive tests'. (a) For X_0 smooth affine one must recover Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology. (b) For X_0 smooth proper with a smooth proper lift X one must recover H_DR(X/S), at least modulo torsion.

In modern terms this is a proposal for a site-theoretic 'dagger/overconvergent' p-adic cohomology. It uses weakly complete lifts instead of PD-envelopes, and is designed to repair the non-commutation of lim with ⊗K. It is the ancestor of rigid cohomology (Berthelot) and especially of Le Stum's overconvergent site.
errors: Not an error but a gap the 'pro' prefix anticipates: the category as described lacks good products. For two W-M lifts B, B' of A_0, B ⊗^† B' -> A_0 has a kernel mod p containing the diagonal ideal, which is not nilpotent. Čech/Alexander-type computations therefore need pro-objects, namely overconvergent neighbourhoods of the diagonal.

Even with pro-objects, a Poincaré lemma after ⊗K needs functions on open tubes (all analytic functions on an open disc, not merely bounded ones). This requires Berthelot-style tubes and strict neighbourhoods. A purely algebraic Zariski site of W-M algebras is unlikely to work as stated. Grothendieck himself calls it a 'first approximation' that will need much softening.
The claim on the previous page that H^i = 0 for i > dim X_0 when X_0 is ordinary is stated without proof. It is plausible if the non-PD site cohomology behaves like Witt vector cohomology.

ideas.what: Diagnosis that infinitesimal/crystalline-without-PD cohomology over W fails because the projective limit does not commute with inverting p.
ideas.modern_name: failure of infinitesimal cohomology in char p; need for divided powers or overconvergence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, IHES 1966, publ. Dix exposés 1968)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés), where failure of the infinitesimal site in char p motivates PD

ideas.what: A site whose objects are W-M (weakly complete) W-algebras B with a surjection to A_0 of nilpotent kernel mod p, with a Zariski-type topology, intended to give a p-adic cohomology of arbitrary X_0.
ideas.modern_name: overconvergent/dagger site; precursor of rigid cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (rigid cohomology, ~1983–86); Le Stum (The overconvergent site, 2007–2011); Grosse-Klönne (dagger spaces, 2000)
ideas.where_published: Possibly a remark on Monsky–Washnitzer in Crystals and de Rham cohomology; no published W-M site known to me

ideas.what: Decisive tests: recover MW cohomology for smooth affine X_0, and de Rham of a smooth proper lift modulo torsion.
ideas.modern_name: comparison theorems rigid = MW and rigid = crystalline ⊗ Q

missed.claim: In 1966–67 Grothendieck proposed, as an alternative to divided powers, a Grothendieck site built from Washnitzer–Monsky weakly complete lifts with nilpotent kernel mod p. The aim was a p-adic cohomology valued in K, with exactly the comparison targets later realised by rigid cohomology. This anticipates the 'overconvergent site' philosophy (Le Stum) by about 40 years and Berthelot's rigid cohomology by about 15 years. Standard historical accounts present crystalline (PD) and MW as Grothendieck's and MW's separate threads, unified by Berthelot.
missed.quote: remplacer le site cristallin par un site plus gros, formé avec des "épaississements" pro [?] infinitésimaux: objets les triples (U_0, V, i : U_0 → V) ... V un affine de W-M sur W
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical credit for the overconvergent-site idea. It also raises a concrete question: can a Zariski-type site of W-M thickenings, allowing pro-objects, compute rigid cohomology without tubes? That is related to recent dagger-algebra and motivic approaches (Vezzani, Ertl, Große-Klönne).

missed.claim: The definition of the topology and of the cohomology on this W-M site is left open, as are the products and pro-objects that are needed. The decisive tests on the next page are never checked here.
missed.quote: Comme topologie, une variante convenable de la zariskienne
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean algebraic (non-rigid-analytic) site computing MW/rigid cohomology for singular or non-liftable X_0 is still of interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a genuinely notable unpublished detail: Grothendieck sketching a dagger/W-M site as a rational p-adic cohomology, with exactly the later rigid-cohomology comparison tests. The idea itself was realised independently later (Berthelot, Le Stum), and the sketch is incomplete.
transcription_corrections: 'immersion nilpotente U_0 → V_{X_0}' should most likely read V_k (or V ×_S Spec k), i.e. the reduction mod p, consistent with 'B/pB → A_0 à noyau nilpotent'.
'du fait que la topologie [?]' is unclear in the image. The sense is 'du fait que ... : la limite projective ne commute pas à la localisation par p'.
'un "[-...-] affine de W-M sur W"' reads as a crossed-out word, then 'affine de W-M sur W'. 'correspondant à une W-M alg.' is probably 'correspondant à une algèbre de W-M B sur W'.
